market_question: Will Dan Cox win the 2026 Maryland Governor Republican primary election?
reasoning: Dan Cox’s 2022 primary win was narrow (52%) despite strong Trump backing, and his catastrophic general election (32%) likely encourages Maryland Republicans to seek a more electable candidate. Although Trump’s endorsement remains influential, the 57.5% market price seems too high given the early stage and the absence of a declared field. I estimate his true chances closer to 45%.
evidence_points: Cox won the 2022 MD-Gov GOP primary with 52.0% over establishment-backed Kelly Schulz (43.8%) after Trump’s endorsement.
In the 2022 general election, Cox was crushed by Wes Moore, 65%–32%, the worst GOP showing in a Maryland governor’s race since 2002.
Given the loss, party insiders and donors may rally behind a more moderate candidate to avoid a repeat, reducing Cox’s probability.
With over a year until the primary, no public polling exists, and the candidate field remains unclear; such uncertainty further dilutes his odds.
sources_consulted: The Baltimore Sun – coverage of Cox’s primary victory and general election loss
Maryland State Board of Elections – official returns
Cook Political Report & Sabato’s Crystal Ball – Maryland race analysis
